title.en: Orbits, Kepler’s Laws & Going to Mars
title.zh: 轨道、开普勒定律与飞向火星

clips.send: Kepler’s 2nd law. Equal areas in equal times. The line from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times (also published in 1609). So a planet moves fastest at perihelion (closest) and slowest at aphelion (farthest). Earth moves about 30.3 km/s in early January and 29.3 km/s in early July. Halley’s Comet races past the Sun at about 55 km/s but crawls at under 1 km/s far beyond Neptune. Newton explained why: gravity pulls straight toward the Sun, so it can speed a planet up or slow it down but never change its “spin” around the Sun (angular momentum stays the same). Close equals short, fat wedge, fast. Far equals long, thin wedge, slow. Same area. Equal areas does not mean equal distances. Near perihelion the planet covers a much longer stretch of its orbit in the same time.

clips.send: Kepler’s 1st law. Orbits are ellipses, with the Sun at one focus. Published in 1609 in Kepler’s book Astronomia Nova (“New Astronomy”). The clue was Mars: Tycho Brahe’s measurements disagreed with a circular orbit by 8 arcminutes, about a quarter of the Moon’s width. Kepler trusted the data and gave up circles. Eccentricity e measures how stretched an ellipse is: 0 is a circle; close to 1 is a long, thin oval. Earth’s e is only 0.017, so its distance from the Sun only changes from about 147 to 152 million km. Ellipse equals two pins + a loop of string. The Sun is one pin. Seasons are NOT caused by Earth getting closer to the Sun: Earth is closest in early January, during northern winter. Seasons come from Earth’s tilt.

clips.send: Kepler’s 3rd law. T squared equals a cubed (years and AU). Published in 1619 in Harmonices Mundi (“The Harmony of the World”). T is the orbital period in years; a is the semi-major axis (half the long axis, the “average” distance) in AU. For every planet, T squared about a cubed . Example: Jupiter, a equals 5.2 AU: a cubed equals 141, so T equals the square root of 141 about 11.9 years. Newton showed the full rule: T squared equals 4 pi squared a cubed divided by (GM), where M is the mass of the central body. Measure a moon’s orbit and you can weigh its planet! Farther out, slower AND a longer path, a much longer year. The law uses a, the average distance (semi-major axis), not the starting distance. Launch from the same spot at different speeds and you get different a and different T.
clips.text: Kepler’s 3rd law. T² = a³ (years and AU). Published in 1619 in Harmonices Mundi (“The Harmony of the World”).. T is the orbital period in years; a is the semi-major axis (half the long axis, the “average” distance) in AU. For every planet, T² ≈ a³.. Example: Jupiter, a = 5.2 AU: a³ = 141, so T = √141 ≈ 11.9 years.. Newton showed the full rule: T² = 4π²a³ ÷ (GM), where M is the mass of the central body. Measure a moon’s orbit and you can weigh its planet!. Farther out → slower AND a longer path → a much longer year.. The law uses a, the average distance (semi-major axis), not the starting distance. Launch from the same spot at different speeds and you get different a and different T.

clips.send: Hohmann transfer. The fuel-saving road between two orbits. Described by German engineer Walter Hohmann in 1925, decades before any spacecraft flew. The transfer orbit is an ellipse with perihelion at Earth’s orbit (1 AU) and aphelion at Mars’s orbit (1.52 AU), so a equals 1.26 AU. By Kepler’s 3rd law its full period is 1.26^1.5 about 1.42 years; the probe flies half of it: about 259 days, or 8.5 months. Real missions often spend a bit more fuel to arrive sooner: Perseverance took about 203 days (launched July 30, 2020, landed February 18, 2021). Speed up at Earth, coast half an ellipse, speed up again at Mars. You don’t aim at where Mars is when you launch. You aim at where Mars WILL BE about 8.5 months later.

clips.send: Newton’s cannon. Orbit equals falling around the planet. Just above Earth’s surface, a circular orbit needs about 7.9 km/s (about 17,700 mph). Higher up, less speed is needed because gravity is weaker there. Escape speed is the square root of 2 about 1.41 times the circular speed: about 11.2 km/s from the surface. The International Space Station flies about 420 km up at about 7.66 km/s and goes around Earth in about 93 minutes. Newton drew this thought experiment in a book published in 1728, just after his death; the law of gravity itself appeared in his Principia (1687). Slow, falls. 7.9 km/s, circle. Faster, ellipse. 11.2 km/s, gone for good. There is plenty of gravity at the space station’s height: about 89 percent of what you feel on the ground. Astronauts float because they are falling together with the station.

clips.send: Launch windows. Every 26 months, Mars is in the right place. Earth laps Mars about once every 780 days (about 26 months). This is called the synodic period. A Hohmann launch needs Mars about 44° ahead of Earth. That lines up for only a few weeks each synodic period. In July 2020 three Mars missions launched within 11 days: the UAE’s Hope, China’s Tianwen-1 and NASA’s Perseverance. Miss the window and you wait about two more years, which is why mission teams work around the clock before a launch. 26 months: two years and two months between chances. Mars is not closest to Earth on launch day. The probe launches months before the two planets are closest, and arrives months after.

clips.send: 牛顿大炮。轨道 等于 绕着行星不停地下落。紧贴地面做圆周运动，需要约 7.9 千米/秒（约每小时 2.8 万千米）。越往高处需要的速度越小，因为那里引力更弱。逃逸速度是圆轨道速度的 根号 2 约等于 1.41 倍：从地面出发约 11.2 千米/秒。国际空间站在约 420 千米高处以约 7.66 千米/秒飞行，大约 93 分钟绕地球一圈。牛顿把这个思想实验画在他去世后不久（1728 年）出版的书里；万有引力定律本身发表在 1687 年的《自然哲学的数学原理》中。慢了，落地；7.9 千米/秒，圆；更快，椭圆；11.2 千米/秒，一去不回。空间站高度的引力并不小：大约是地面的 百分之89。宇航员飘浮，是因为他们和空间站一起在下落。

clips.send: 开普勒第二定律。相同时间扫过相同面积。从太阳到行星的连线在相同时间内扫过相同的面积（也在 1609 年发表）。所以行星在近日点最快、远日点最慢。地球 1 月初约 30.3 千米/秒，7 月初约 29.3 千米/秒。哈雷彗星掠过太阳时约 55 千米/秒，到了海王星以外却慢到不足 1 千米/秒。牛顿解释了原因：引力始终指向太阳，只能让行星加速或减速，却不能改变它绕太阳“转动”的量（角动量守恒）。近 等于 又短又胖的扇形、快；远 等于 又细又长的扇形、慢；面积一样。面积相等不等于路程相等。在近日点附近，行星在同样的时间里走过的路长得多。

clips.send: 霍曼转移轨道。两条轨道之间最省燃料的路。德国工程师瓦尔特·霍曼在 1925 年提出，比第一颗人造卫星早了几十年。转移轨道是一个椭圆：近日点在地球轨道（1 天文单位），远日点在火星轨道（1.52 天文单位），所以 a 等于 1.26 天文单位。根据开普勒第三定律，它绕一整圈要 1.26^1.5 约等于 1.42 年；探测器只飞半圈：约 259 天，即 8.5 个月。真实任务常多花一点燃料以便早点到达：毅力号大约飞了 203 天（2020 年 7 月 30 日发射，2021 年 2 月 18 日着陆）。在地球处加速，滑行半个椭圆，到火星再加速。发射时不是瞄准火星现在的位置，而是瞄准火星 8.5 个月后会在的位置。

clips.send: 发射窗口。每 26 个月火星才会到达合适的位置。地球大约每 780 天（约 26 个月）“套圈”火星一次，这叫会合周期。霍曼转移发射时，火星需要领先地球约 44 度 ，每个会合周期只有几周符合条件。2020 年 7 月，11 天之内有三个火星任务先后发射：阿联酋的“希望号”、中国的“天问一号”和 NASA 的毅力号。错过窗口就要再等约两年，所以发射前任务团队总是争分夺秒。26 个月：两年零两个月才有一次机会。发射那天火星并不是离地球最近。探测器在两颗行星最接近之前几个月出发，之后几个月才到达。

clips.send: 开普勒第三定律。T 的平方 等于 a 的立方 （年和天文单位）。1619 年发表在《世界的和谐》中。T 是公转周期（年），a 是半长轴（长轴的一半，相当于“平均距离”，单位天文单位）。对每颗行星都有 T 的平方 约等于 a 的立方 。例：木星 a 等于 5.2 天文单位，a 的立方 等于 141，所以 T 等于 根号 141 约等于 11.9 年。牛顿给出了完整公式：T 的平方 等于 4 派 的平方 a 的立方 除以 （GM），M 是中心天体的质量。测出卫星的轨道，就能“称出”行星的质量！离得越远，跑得越慢、路也越长，一年长得多。定律里用的是半长轴 a（平均距离），不是出发点的距离。从同一点以不同速度发射，得到的 a 和 T 都不同。
clips.text: 开普勒第三定律. T² = a³（年和天文单位）. 1619 年发表在《世界的和谐》中。. T 是公转周期（年），a 是半长轴（长轴的一半，相当于“平均距离”，单位天文单位）。对每颗行星都有 T² ≈ a³。. 例：木星 a = 5.2 天文单位，a³ = 141，所以 T = √141 ≈ 11.9 年。. 牛顿给出了完整公式：T² = 4π²a³ ÷ （GM），M 是中心天体的质量。测出卫星的轨道，就能“称出”行星的质量！. 离得越远 → 跑得越慢、路也越长 → 一年长得多。. 定律里用的是半长轴 a（平均距离），不是出发点的距离。从同一点以不同速度发射，得到的 a 和 T 都不同。

clips.send: 开普勒第一定律。轨道是椭圆，太阳在一个焦点上。1609 年发表在开普勒的《新天文学》一书中。线索来自火星：第谷的测量和圆形轨道差了 8 角分，大约是月亮宽度的四分之一。开普勒相信数据，放弃了圆。偏心率 e 表示椭圆有多扁：0 是圆；接近 1 就是又细又长的椭圆。地球的 e 只有 0.017，它到太阳的距离只在约 1.47 亿到 1.52 亿千米之间变化。椭圆 等于 两枚图钉 + 一圈线。太阳就是其中一枚图钉。季节不是因为地球离太阳近了：地球在 1 月初离太阳最近，那时北半球正是冬天。季节来自地轴倾斜。
